endorsements.quote: Transparent description of the data and its context needs to be available as metadata to any developer of AI tools or other secondary users of data, whether within the LHS or an external dataset contributed to by the LHS, to ensure developers address health inequalities.
It is essential that AI healthcare technologies are developed using datasets that represent the intended use population, with deliberate consideration of contextualized groups of interest.

unlisted_practices: Learning health systems should adopt the STANDING Together recommendations as a key learning cycle for transparent reporting of dataset curation and use.

Dataset curators should provide accompanying documentation for all health datasets covering provenance, purpose, sampling, demographic groups, potential bias sources, data shifts, ethics, and governance.
Learning health systems should track representation, errors, and missingness in data collection and AI implementation to support responsible decision making.
Learning health systems should understand health disparities in their population and ensure collected data are fit to describe and address them.
Developers and implementers should report omissions in meeting transparency recommendations along with their reasoning.
Users of the STANDING Together recommendations should publish their implementation experiences to support community learning.

screen.reason: This paper presents the STANDING Together recommendations/framework for reporting and mitigating bias in health AI data within Learning Health Systems.
